statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registration System (CORES) operated by Service Alberta; official portal: https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporation names must be in English or French unless an English or French version is used for the legal name; names are required to be in Latin script without diacritical marks that could create confusion in registry searches; corporate suffixes and legal elements must follow the recognized form for the entity type, including 'Unlimited' or 'ULC' for an unlimited liability corporation under Alberta law.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, within the applicable statutory review period, setting out the grounds why the proposed name should be accepted. The Director will reconsider the name in accordance with the Alberta Business Corporations Act and regulations. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review under the relevant Alberta corporate legislation. A new or reserved NUANS name search report is required before any appeal or resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable for registered office purposes only if it provides a real, physical street address in Alberta and service of process can be effected at that address during normal business hours; a post office box or shared-only mail drop without a physical reception capacity is not permissible. The MMORPG publisher's online-only commercial substance does not require a local operational facility, but the registered office address must remain accessible for service and regulatory correspondence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated below 10%) for a hardcore MMORPG online publisher with no statutory license, no physical inventory, and no on-premises retail or storage functions; an unannounced on-site inspection is unlikely unless triggered by a complaint, AML/CFT filing, or a tax authority verification event.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended; incorporation under s. 6; unlimited liability corporation provisions under ss. 15.1–15.6; registered office under s. 104; directors and officers under Part 8.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account rule; the ULC may incorporate with nil paid-up capital or nominal subscribed capital. Shareholder liability is unlimited in accordance with the ULC provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors of [the Company], having been duly constituted, adopted the following resolutions: 1. Share Subscription. RESOLVED that the subscription of [Founder] for 100 Class A Common Shares, no par value, at CAD 1.00 per share, is accepted, and that [Founder] is issued such shares upon full payment. 2. Registered Office. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company is established at [Registered Address], Calgary, Alberta, and that such address is filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry. 3. Officers. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an accredited NUANS service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed corporate name, ensuring the distinctive element is followed by the legal element 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company'. Reserve the proposed name with the Alberta Corporate Registry for up to 90 days to prevent another entity from accepting the same name during the incorporation process.
required_dossiers: Proposed name with ULC legal element
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is not distinct or is confusingly similar, submit a revised name for a further NUANS search or obtain prior consent from the conflicting name holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles, Notices, and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, including the unlimited liability statement, share structure, restrictions on business, and number of directors. Prepare the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors. Obtain signed director consents from each proposed director.
required_dossiers: NUANS Search Report and name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any drafting deficiency and refile the affected instrument with the Alberta Corporate Registry; legal counsel may submit a supplementary affidavit to cure formal defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Pay Statutory Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Service Alberta Online Registry Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office, and Notice of Directors electronically or in person with the Alberta Corporate Registry. Pay the applicable statutory filing fee and retain the transaction receipt. Electronic filing does not require notarization of the signed documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry deficiency letter within the stated period, usually 30 days, by filing corrected documents or providing additional clarifications; refiling may require a supplementary fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and Registry Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review, the Alberta Corporate Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the legal name, jurisdiction, incorporation date, and corporate ID number. Obtain a corporate registry search or certified extract to confirm the ULC's active status.
required_dossiers: Corporate registry search report for verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error or incorrect corporate ID, apply for a correction of record under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, with supporting evidence of the error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold First Board Meeting and Adopt Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in accordance with the bylaws and applicable corporate law. Adopt the first board resolution approving share subscription, the registered office address, and officer appointments. Record the minutes, issue share certificates, and enter the resolution into the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice and first board meeting minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director or officer appointment is found deficient, the incorporator and validly appointed directors may pass a curative resolution or call a shareholders' meeting to ratify appointments and validate the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for CRA Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC for a 15-digit Business Number with the Canada Revenue Agency and request the applicable program accounts, including corporate income tax, GST/HST, and the import/export account if needed. For a global MMORPG publisher with Apple App Store and Google Play payouts, assess obligations for GST/HST on digital supplies and corporate income tax reporting for non-resident revenue streams.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Number is not activated within the projected timeline, contact the CRA business account line to verify the registration and submit any outstanding documentation; retain a copy of the submitted registration as evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing, physical production, or facility-based processing is undertaken by a software publisher.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required; a municipal business licence and the CRA Business Number registration are sufficient for commercial operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable — Alberta Environment and Protected Areas does not require an EIA for MMORPG software publishing with no physical undertaking.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — non-industrial digital publishing activity without construction, land disturbance, discharge, or waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or air-emission thresholds apply. If the company later owns or operates a data center, then applicable Alberta environmental and municipal electrical mechanical codes must be assessed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For leased office premises only: fire safety certification and occupancy permit under the Alberta Safety Codes Act, together with workplace health and safety clearance under Alberta Occupational Health and Safety legislation. No civil defense certificate is required for a digital MMORPG publishing entity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC). Primary portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) and CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html). Alberta corporate income tax is administered federally by the CRA under a federal-provincial tax-collection agreement; there is no separate Alberta corporate tax authority. Alberta Corporate Registry handles corporate law filings only and is not a tax authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta ULC must obtain a nine-digit federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA. Procedure: (1) register via Business Registration Online (BRO), by paper Form RC1, or through a CRA-authorized representative; (2) the BN automatically activates a Corporation Income Tax account (RC) — mandatory for every corporation resident in Canada, with T2 Corporation Income Tax Return due within six months after fiscal year-end and tax balances due within two months (or three months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation eligible for the small business deduction); (3) open a GST/HST account (RT) once taxable worldwide revenues exceed the CAD $30,000 registration threshold; (4) open a payroll deductions account (RP) when employees are engaged; (5) complete Alberta corporate law incorporation and initial notice filings with the Alberta Corporate Registry, obtaining the Alberta corporate access number, which is separate from the CRA BN. Non-resident officers or directors may appoint a Canadian authorized representative using Form RC59/RC461 and must provide the ULC's foreign mailing address. If the ULC is fiscally transparent under US check-the-box rules, the US shareholder should file Form 8832 and notify the CRA of the resulting classification to align Canadian and US filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — an Alberta ULC is mandatorily a corporation and a resident of Canada for Canadian Income Tax Act Part I and Alberta corporate tax purposes (a taxable Canadian corporation), but it is eligible for pass-through treatment at the shareholder level for US federal tax purposes: a single-member ULC may be treated as a disregarded entity and a multi-member ULC as a partnership under US check-the-box rules unless an affirmative corporate-classification election is made. For GST/HST, the ULC is a separate person from its shareholders; no fiscal transparency or consolidation override is permitted under the Excise Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include: (1) US IRC Form 8832 check-the-box election to classify the ULC as an association taxable as a corporation, as a partnership, or as a disregarded entity; (2) Canada-US Tax Convention Article IV(6) election, filed by written notification to the CRA competent authority, under which a Canadian unlimited liability company that is fiscally transparent for US tax purposes may be treated as a resident of Canada for all purposes of the Convention, thereby preserving treaty benefits on cross-border payments; (3) Excise Tax Act section 239 small-supplier relief for non-resident digital-service suppliers before mandatory GST/HST registration; (4) Income Tax Act section 216 election for non-resident passive income and services where applicable; (5) allocation of the CAD $500,000 small-business deduction limit among associated corporations; and (6) hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act sections 18.2, 18.3 and 18.4, which are mandatory rather than elective and disallow deductions to the extent of the resulting US-Canadian hybrid mismatch.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax, Canada's federal value-added tax. Alberta imposes no provincial retail sales tax and no provincial component in the HST, so the applicable system in Alberta is the 5% federal GST only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 in total annual worldwide taxable supplies. Mandatory registration is triggered when taxable supplies exceed CAD $30,000 either in a single calendar quarter or over 12 consecutive months; registration must be applied for within 29 days after the month or quarter of the excess. Alberta uses the identical federal threshold because no provincial component applies. Small suppliers below the threshold may voluntarily register to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, digital stamping, or government pre-approval of individual e-invoices. E-invoicing is permitted, and the Pan-Canadian Peppol interoperability framework and the federal e-invoicing service are available on an opt-in basis. The ULC's practical compliance duties are: (1) issue GST/HST tax invoices with the prescribed information for B2B supply chains under ETA sections 169 and 170; (2) rely on simplified invoices and net settlement reports for Apple App Store and Google Play consumer transactions; (3) file GST/HST returns electronically via Form GST34 using GST/HST NETFILE or CRA My Business Account on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis depending on annual revenue; and (4) retain electronic source records, including platform payout statements, subscriber IP logs, purchase transaction files, and currency conversion records, for six years under ETA section 286 and Income Tax Act section 230.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% GST/HST applies to the ULC's MMORPG digital exports under ETA Schedule VI, Part V (sections 21, 22 and 23) where: the recipient is a non-resident not present in Canada at the time of supply; the digital content is delivered to a destination outside Canada; and the services are performed wholly outside Canada. In-app virtual currency, consumables, and game entitlements sold through Apple App Store and Google Play are zero-rated only with documented proof that each end-customer is a non-resident, that the download and gameplay occur offshore, and that the platform remittances constitute foreign-source consideration. Sales to Canadian consumers remain taxable at 5% GST. Effective July 1, 2021, the ETA digital-economy marketplace rules (sections 18.1 and 18.2) may deem the online platform operator, rather than the ULC, to be the supplier of digital services to Canadian consumers; the ULC must map the contractual billing flow to confirm whether it or Apple/Google is the deemed supplier of the Canadian portion, and whether zero-rating applies to offshore B2B channel sales.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency electronic export declaration / B13A) — required for tangible media shipments; for pure digital MMORPG downloads, retain a digital export record instead
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing physical export of promotional or collector-box media, with server-side download logs and IP geolocation records substituting for digital deliveries
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank credit advices, and FX conversion records evidencing offshore consideration received from Apple and Google
Apple App Store and Google Play consolidated monthly payout statements showing gross sales, store-level apportionment, country-level download counts, and net settlement amounts
Subscriber licensing agreements, terms-of-service acceptance records, and digital delivery confirmations demonstrating non-resident end-user status
Server access logs, IP geolocation reports, and content-delivery-network delivery data evidencing offshore enjoyment of digital content
Zero-rated tax invoices, B2B recipients' value-added tax registration numbers, and online-marketplace supporting schedules for any zero-rated self-assessment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit scrutiny of zero-rated digital exports is elevated: the supplier bears the burden of proving export entitlement, and failure to maintain the contemporaneous documentation bundle triggers reassessment of the supply at 5% GST with compound daily interest. Fraudulent or grossly negligent zero-rating claims attract: a 30% gross-negligence penalty under ETA section 285(1); wilful-evasion penalties up to 200% of the net tax sought to be evaded; summary conviction fines up to CAD $25,000 and imprisonment up to two years, or indictment fines up to CAD $100,000 and imprisonment up to five years; and an eight-year limitation-period extension for misrepresentation under ETA section 298. Retrospective clawback also cancels any input tax credits claimed on related inputs and permits reopening of prior returns, recharacterization of offshore platform receipts as Canadian-source royalties or service revenue under transfer-pricing rules (Income Tax Act section 247), and imposition of associated hybrid-mismatch disallowances. Directors of a ULC may be assessed jointly and severally for unremitted or fraudulently claim-adjusted GST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential regulation by Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); money laundering supervision by Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. No exchange control legislation, approval requirements, or profit-remittance hurdles apply. The Alberta ULC may repatriate profits, pay dividends, return capital, and service foreign debt in CAD or any freely convertible currency, subject only to withholding tax under the Income Tax Act and reporting obligations under exchange control statistics reporting to Statistics Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, forced conversion, or prescribed timeline for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency domestically or abroad. Reporting burdens apply only where a single transaction exceeds C$10,000 or where patterns of transactions trigger FINTRAC large-value reporting; no proportionality ratio or conversion mandate exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Canada does not issue a dedicated electronic-money-institution (EMI) licence. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Payoneer may operate in Canada only as money services businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC or as authorized foreign money remitters under provincial remittance regimes. They may support USD/CAD conversions for MMORPG payouts from Apple and Google, but they are not deposit-taking institutions; their use should be strictly limited to settlement accelerators rather than primary treasury accounts. Primary liquidity must rest with federally regulated chartered banks due to improved protection under the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) and OSFI liquidity standards.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks generally permit remote corporate onboarding through OSFI-compliant video KYC and digital verification tools. Directors and beneficial owners are not statutorily required to appear physically except where bank internal risk policy overrides for unlimited liability entities or for directors resident in high-risk jurisdictions. In practice, Big Six Canadian banks accept a fully virtual onboarding path using certified passport scans, apostilled corporate documents, and a live teleconference or video interview. Final account activation may require a notarized resolution and a sworn ULC declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC unlimited liability structure with non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation with share conditions, articles of incorporation, register of directors and shareholders, executed ULC declaration of unlimited liability, ownership-chain diagram, copies of trust deeds if nominee shareholder exists, and proof of economic substance (Alberta registered office, tax filings, operating agreements).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual currency/gaming risk flag on in-app purchase monetization
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/ATF policy, transaction monitoring system details, evidence of no peer-to-peer cash-out mechanism, Apple/App Store and Google Play distribution agreements, provider payout statements, historical settlement ledger, and game economy design documentation demonstrating absence of laundering features.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds concerns for inbound capital contributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreements, bank statements of contributing shareholders, proof of source of wealth (tax returns, sale contracts, inheritance or trust documents), notarized declarations from shareholders, and legal opinions from counsel in the contributor's jurisdiction.

Completed AML onboarding questionnaires, sanctions and PEP screening results (OFAC, EU, UN, Canadian SEMA lists), beneficial ownership disclosure forms, nationality and residence information for all directors, certifications from online verification providers, and board resolutions confirming prohibition of prohibited persons.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections into the Alberta ULC may be transmitted from foreign banks via SWIFT MT103 using explanatory remittance information and, where requested by the receiving Canadian bank, an internal source-of-funds questionnaire. Canada does not impose statutory SWIFT purpose codes; however, reference to 'Capital Contribution', 'Equity Injection', or 'Paid-in Capital' should be inserted into the remittance narrative (field 70). For USD-denominated injections, the Canadian bank will route to its US correspondent (e.g., RBC Bank (Georgia), TD Bank US). Verification evidence includes the share subscription agreement and a resolution of directors authorizing receipt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for vendor payments, royalty distributions, marketing expenses, and developer profit participations are cleared via SWIFT MT103 (cross-border), Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for Canadian-dollar domestic wires, and LN/GRO (Fedwire) or CHIPS correspondents for USD payments. For trade finance with offline distributors, Canadian banks issue commercial letters of credit pursuant to UCP 600 and may process sight drafts or deferred-payment LCs. Apple and Google payout receivables are swept via ABA routing from Stripe Mexico? Actually from Apple's and Google's payment rails directly into the ULC's USD account at a Canadian bank correspondent; then converted to CAD by standing instructions or managed market orders.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with maturities up to 12 months
FX swaps (swap of principal and interest flows in CAD/USD)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (for funded debt positions)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for pair exposures involving emerging-market currencies not clearing in Canada (CAD/USD trades on a deliverable basis)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (corporate annual declaration under section 115 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an additional CAD 125 late filing fee; continued non-compliance may result in administrative strike-off/dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta provincial corporate tax integrated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Edmonton Tax Centre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance of tax generally payable within 2 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, arbitrary assessment by CRA, and possible prosecution under section 238 of the Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a private non-reporting issuer ULC has no revenue/asset threshold mandating an independent audit; an auditor may be waived by shareholder resolution for each financial year. An audit becomes compulsory if the corporation is a reporting issuer under securities law, if the articles require it, or if the shareholders do not pass an annual waiver resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian private enterprise GAAP (ASPE) as permitted for a private ULC; CPA Canada Handbook governs preparation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Alberta Annual Return filed within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary constitutes the annual confirmation of registered office, directors, officers, and shareholders. Share transfers are effective only upon registration in the Register of Members; the register must be brought up to date before the annual return is submitted. Any applicable federal significant-control transparency requirements must be satisfied on a continuing basis through an internal individual transparency register if the entity falls within the scope of Canadian corporate beneficial-ownership legislation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150 - US$600 per year for professional registered office and corporate agent services in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 - US$12,000 for a full statutory audit; US$2,000 - US$5,000 for a review engagement

stage_6.entry_description: Corporation name, BN, fiscal year-end, RC0001 tax account, residency, type of corporation (Alberta ULC — taxable Canadian corporation), ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210, mmorpg publisher.
